# Kiṁsīla Sutta (Snp 2.9 (PTS Snp 56))
**ID:** Snp 2.9 (PTS Snp 56)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kiṁsīla Sutta* (Snp 2.9) is the ninth discourse in the Cūḷavagga of the *Suttanipāta*, comprising verses 324–330 (PTS p. 56) [Müller 1881; Anderson and Smith 1913; Norman 1997-2001]. Metrically, the discourse is composed primarily in Triṣṭubh and mixed Triṣṭubh/Jagatī metres, alongside a mixed Triṣṭubh/Śloka verse (verse 327) and Śloka [Norman 1997-2001]. S.M. Katre identifies the sutta as an early Buddhist moral ballad aimed at inculcating ethical precepts [Katre 1931].
Opening with an inquiry concerning what kind of morality (*kimsīla*), conduct (*kimsamācāra*), and actions enable a person to become properly grounded and attain the ultimate goal (*uttamattha*) [Katre 1931; Anderson and Smith 1913], the sutta delineates the qualities and behaviors required to learn and reap the full benefit of the Dhamma [SuttaCentral]. It emphasizes respect for elders, attentive and timely listening to well-spoken Dhamma discourses, and the mastery of tranquil understanding free from sloth, pride, and heedlessness [Müller 1881; Norman 1997-2001; Anderson and Smith 1913].
The text is commented upon in the *Paramatthajotikā II* (Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā), which is also reflected in Pali-internal text reuse identified by DharmaNexus [Norman 1997-2001; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes a resembling parallel in the *Sumaṅgalajātaka* (Ja 420) [SuttaCentral]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies automatic cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Udānavarga* (including the Subaši Sanskrit manuscript and Tibetan canonical editions D0326 and D4099), as well as minor alignments with later Tibetan treatises such as the *Mahābhadantaśrīghoṣapreṣitabhoṭasvāmidāsasārasaṃgrahalekha* (D4355) [DharmaNexus].
